newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance minister says resign talk baseless.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance minister says resign talk baseless.

text.p: Thailand's Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan has no plans to resign despite speculation he would do so if his policies on sweeping budget cuts were not backed by the government, a government spokeswoman said on Monday. He has never voiced any desire to resign and the recent budget cuts were well-supported by members of Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's coalition government, she quoted the minister as saying by telephone from Hong Kong where he is currently on a business trip.
Thai financial markets were totally unaffected by the speculation reported in a Thai newspaper.
The baht was quoted at the day's high against the dollar at 25.908/25.910 at 0650 GMT compared with 25.924/25.929 early in the morning, dealers said.
The Thai stock index closed at the midday break down 4.47 points to 743.23. Traders attributed the weakness to profit-taking after last week's rally.

Government spokeswoman Kanala Khantaprab denied speculation that Amnuay was unhappy and that he allegedly had not obtained full cooperation from cabinet members on budget cuts and policies to tackle economic problems initiated by him.
"Dr. Amnuay has sent a message to us from Hong Kong to confirm that he did not have any intention to resign at all," she said
Amnuay planned to give a news conference on Tuesday when he returned from Hong Kong to reiterate his plan to remain in his job and to deny the rumour carried by the press.
